title: The Two Pots
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: Two Pots, one of earthenware and the other of brass, were carried away down a river in flood. The Brazen Pot urged his companion to keep close by his side, and he would protect him. The other thanked him, but begged him not to come near him on any account: "For that," he said, "is just what I am most afraid of. One touch from you and I should be broken in pieces."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what are the two Pots made of?
options: Wood and iron
Clay and glass
Earthenware and brass
Silver and copper

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how do the two Pots come to be carried down the river?
options: The river was in flood
A boat carrying them capsized
A storm blew them off a shelf into the water
A merchant dropped them from a bridge

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Brazen Pot urge his companion to do?
options: Float ahead of him to check for danger
Call out for help from the riverbank
Hold on tightly to a passing branch
Keep close by his side, so he can protect him

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Earthenware Pot beg the Brazen Pot not to do?
options: Speak so loudly in the water
Come near him on any account
Leave him alone in the current
Reach the shore before he does

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Earthenware Pot say he is most afraid of?
options: Sinking to the bottom of the river
Being swept too far from home
Being touched by the Brazen Pot and broken in pieces
Losing sight of the Brazen Pot

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is the Brazen Pot's offer of protection actually risky for the Earthenware Pot?
options: The very closeness meant to protect him could shatter his fragile material instead
The Brazen Pot secretly wants to sink the Earthenware Pot
The river current would push them apart no matter what
The Earthenware Pot cannot swim as well as the Brazen Pot

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Earthenware Pot understand about his own nature that the Brazen Pot may not fully consider?
options: That he is actually the stronger of the two
That he does not need any protection at all
That he was made by a different craftsman
That he is far more fragile than his companion

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "Brazen" mean in "The Brazen Pot"?
options: Extremely bold or shameless
Made of brass
Painted a bright color
Very old and cracked

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Pots were carried away "in flood"?
options: The river had frozen over completely
The river was unusually calm and still
The river was swollen and overflowing with water
The river had run dry in places

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: A partnership between very different kinds of things can put the weaker one at risk
Rivers in flood are too dangerous for any pot to survive
Brass is always a better material than earthenware
True friends should always stay as close as possible

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Earthenware Pot respond to the offer of protection?
options: He gladly accepts and moves closer at once
He ignores the offer and drifts silently away
He asks for a different kind of help instead
He thanks the Brazen Pot but declines the offer

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Brazen Pot promise to do if the other stays close?
options: Guide him to the shore
Protect him
Warn him of rocks ahead
Carry him out of the water

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is the immediate cause of the two Pots being swept away together?
options: A sudden storm at sea
A boat that overturned
A river in flood
A bridge that collapsed

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Earthenware Pot's caution seem wiser than it might first appear?
options: It protects him from a danger the well-meaning Brazen Pot does not fully grasp
It shows he does not trust the Brazen Pot's intentions at all
It proves he wants to be swept away alone
It reveals that he secretly dislikes the Brazen Pot

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what mismatch between the two Pots creates the danger in the first place?
options: One floats while the other tends to sink
One is much larger than the other
One belongs to a different owner than the other
One is fragile and the other is hard enough to break it on contact

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "on any account" mean in "not to come near him on any account"?
options: Only during the daytime
Under no circumstances at all
As often as possible
Only if truly necessary

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: Two Pots work together and safely reach the shore
A Pot made of brass is broken by the river current
A fragile Pot refuses a sturdier Pot's offer of closeness, fearing it would be destroyed
Two Pots argue over which material is stronger
